newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: MAM vice-chairman favours UK and Japan.
newsitem.headline: MAM vice-chairman favours UK and Japan.

text.p: The most promising outlooks for international investors were in the UK and Japan, vice-chairman of Mercury Asset Management, Richard Dawes, said on Thursday.
He was cautious about the rest of the Pacific and international bonds, did not like the mark and was concerned about the United States and Europe.
Dawes was addressing the management and clients of Botswana Insurance, whose global fund Mercury manages.

In the fixed interest markets, it was clear that the UK interest rate cycle had turned and sterling was expected to outperform other European currencies, Dawes said. The UK economy was strengthening and corporate balance sheets were strong.
"The Bank of England will raise interest rates aggressively," Dawes said. "The European common currency will most likely be established without England. It will be weak."
In Japan, he expected present low interest rates to be maintained, but the future yen-dollar rate was critical.
Commenting on other markets, Dawes said the U.S. appeared overvalued.
In Europe there was concern over the proposed common currency. "There has been a recovery in corporate profits in France and Germany, but unemployment remains high," Dawes said.
The Pacific region remained vulnerable to U.S. interest rate rises.
He was also cautious about international bonds, because interest rates were rising, but considered UK bonds basically strong.
On the currency markets, Dawes said: "Sterling and the U.S. dollar are okay, but we do not like the deutschemark at the moment. It will weaken if the European currency unit goes ahead as proposed."
